declaration.question: with random blocks, does the multilevel gain survive (a) a random tie sign instead of the tautology rule, (b) a random restart of the coarsest level instead of projection
declaration.statistic: first-hit solved count per n (20 instances, budget 60000), median evaluations over solved runs with solved fraction beside it; same instances and seeds as EDG_001. Not blind: EDG_001's ml_random column (9/20 at n=60) was seen first
declaration.discriminates: each arm differs from ml_random by one switch, so a gap names that switch; ml_random is rerun here as the control and must reproduce EDG_001's column exactly
declaration.expected: a switch CARRIES the gain if its arm solves >= 3/20 fewer than ml_random at n=60, or at n=52 and n=60 both by >= 2. Falsifier (EDG_006 as written): both arms within 2/20 of ml_random at every n >= 44, leaving the smaller coarse variable count as the remaining candidate. Prior lean, stated so it can be wrong: the sign rule carries more than projection, because random pairs share a clause often at these densities and the rule then removes clauses
